p1.original: 7.1 新生儿具有某些先天的能力，这些能力可以帮助他们找到营养物质、回避危险情境，以及与他人互动——所有这些能力都有助于他们生存下去。
p1.en: 7.1 Newborn children have certain congenital abilities that help them find nutrients, avoid dangerous situations and interact with others — all of which help them survive.

p2.original: 7.2 先天和后天因素的共同作用帮助儿童掌握重要的发展任务，特别是在语言习得、认知发展和社会关系发展等领域。
p2.en: 7.2 The combined role of congenital and acquired factors helps children to take on important developmental tasks, especially in the areas of language acquisition, cognitive development and the development of social relations.

p3.original: 7.3 个体在青春期会因生理变化、认知变化和社会情绪压力等面临新的发展挑战。
p3.en: 7.3 Individuals face new development challenges during adolescence due to physical, cognitive and social stress.

p4.original: 7.4 在成年期，人们将完成一系列的转变。在此过程中，先天和后天因素继续相互作用，不同年龄的文化规范和最新技术相结合，以此提升成年人的生活质量并延长其寿命。
p4.en: 7.4 In adulthood, a series of transformations will be completed. In this process, the innate and acquired factors continue to interact, combining cultural norms of different ages with the latest technologies, as a means of improving the quality of life of adults and extending their longevity.

p5.original: 一对双胞胎在出生时就被分开了，直到长大成人才再次重逢。没有什么比这样的故事更能吸引媒体的关注了。美国明尼苏达大学（University of Minnesota）的心理学家托马斯·布沙尔（Thomas Bouchard）主持的著名的双生子研究项目提供了大量的这类故事。记者们争相报道的是那些失散多年的同卵双胞胎之间不可思议的相似性。要知道，他们是由不同的父母养大成人，并接受了不同老师的教育，受到不同的同伴和兄弟姐妹的影响，甚至有时成长于不同的文化背景中。
p5.en: A pair of twins was separated at birth and not re-emergence until they had grown up. There's nothing more interesting than a story like that. The well-known twin-child research project sponsored by Thomas Bouchard, a psychologist at the University of Minnesota, United States of America, provides a wealth of such stories. The journalists argued about the incredible similarities between the same twins who had been separated for years. They are raised by different parents and are educated by different teachers, influenced by different peers and siblings, and sometimes even in different cultural contexts.

p6.original: 以“吉姆（Jim）双胞胎”为例，同卵双胞胎吉姆·斯普林格（Jim Springer）和吉姆·刘易斯（Jim Lewis）出生几周后就由不同的人收养，并且在不同的地方长大。虽然在39岁之前他们的人生之路再无交集，但是仿佛有什么东西驱使他们走在相似的道路上。当他们再次相逢时，这对“吉姆双胞胎”发现他们的习惯、偏好和经历有很多相似之处，这令人非常惊讶。
p6.en: In the case of the Jim twins, Jim Springer and Jim Lewis were adopted by different people and raised in different places a few weeks after their birth. Although their lives had never been crossed before they were 39, it seemed that something had driven them along similar paths. When they met again, it was surprising that the “Jim twins” found many similarities between their habits, preferences and experiences.

p7.original: 他们在性格、智力、态度和兴趣方面的测试得分几乎相同。
p7.en: Their test scores are almost identical in character, intelligence, attitude and interest.

p8.original: 健康方面，两个人的血压都有点高，并且在一段时间内都被误以为患有心脏病。两个人都做过输精管结扎手术，并且都有偏头痛。
p8.en: In terms of health, both men had a slightly high blood pressure and had been mistaken for heart disease for some time. Both had vasectomy and had migraines.

p9.original: 两个人都是“老烟枪”，都抽沙龙（Salem）香烟。两个人都喝米勒（Miller）淡啤。
p9.en: Both men were “old smokers” and smoked a salon (Salem). Both of them drank Miller light beer.

p10.original: 上学期间，两个人都是不爱学习的学生：吉姆·刘易斯在10年级时退学，而吉姆·斯普林格挣扎到高中毕业。
p10.en: During the school year, both of them were students who did not want to study: Jim Lewis dropped out of grade 10 and Jim Springer struggled to graduate from high school.

p11.original: 两个人都结过两次婚，并且第一任妻子的名字都叫琳达（Linda）。两个人的第二任妻子都叫贝蒂（Betty）。两个人都喜欢在家里到处留便条来表达爱意。
p11.en: Both were married twice and the first wife was named Linda. The second wife of both was Betty. Both people like to leave notes around their homes to express their love.

p12.original: 刘易斯有3个儿子，其中一个儿子的名字是詹姆斯·艾伦（James Alan）。斯普林格有3个女儿和1个儿子，他儿子的名字也是詹姆斯·艾伦。
p12.en: Lewis has three sons, one of whom is named James Alan. Springer has three daughters and one son, whose name is also James Allen.

p13.original: 两个人都养了一条叫托伊的狗。
p13.en: Both had a dog named Toy.

p14.original: 两个人都开雪佛兰汽车，喜欢咬指甲，喜欢改装车比赛，不喜欢棒球。
p14.en: Both drive Chevy, likes to bite nails, likes to change cars, don't like baseball.

p15.original: 两个人都曾做过副警长。

p16.original: 两个人都有做木工的爱好。刘易斯喜欢做小的野餐桌，斯普林格喜欢做小摇椅。两个人都曾制作过白色长凳，并且将其安置在院子里的树下。
p16.en: Both people have a hobby for woodwork. Lewis likes to make little picnic tables, Springer likes to make little rocking chairs. Both men had made white benches and placed them under trees in the yard.

p17.original: 当布沙尔从报纸上第一次读到吉姆兄弟的故事时，他意识到他们的故事是一次难得的机会。他可以通过这类案例来研究遗传和环境的相对作用，以及在个体成长的过程中，它们的作用是如何随时间逐渐展开的（Holden，1980a，1980b；Lykken et al.，1992）。吉姆兄弟同意参加这个研究项目，并且成为115对参与研究的被分开抚养的双胞胎中的第一对（加上4组分开抚养的三胞胎），他们在明尼苏达大学接受了20多年的研究。
p17.en: When Bouchar read the story of the Jim brothers for the first time in the newspaper, he realized that their story was a rare opportunity. He can study the relative effects of genetic and environmental effects in such cases and how their effects are evolving over time in the process of individual growth (Holden, 1980a, 1980b); Lykken et al., 1992. The Jim brothers agreed to participate in the research project and became the first pair of 115 separated twins (plus four separated triplets) who participated in the study, who were studied at Minnesota University for more than 20 years.

p18.original: 另一对引人注目的双胞胎是奥斯卡·斯托（Oskar Stör）和杰克·尤菲（Jack Yufe）。他们也是从出生起就被分开了，并且自那以后，他们的人生走向了几乎完全不同的方向。斯托由他在捷克斯洛伐克的外婆养大，并且在第二次世界大战期间进入了纳粹办的学校；而尤菲被他的生父带到了特立尼达，并成为一名犹太教徒。斯托已经结婚了，是一名坚定的工会参与者，并且热衷于滑雪；而尤菲正在分居中，是一名商人，并且自认为是一个工作狂。除了这些明显的差异，研究人员发现两个人在某些微小的行为模式上具有惊人的相似性。两个人都留着修剪整齐的胡子，都从后往前看杂志，都习惯在手腕上戴橡皮筋，都会先冲马桶再上厕所，都喜欢在咖啡中加入黄油吐司，都觉得在公众场合大声打喷嚏很有趣。
p18.en: Another striking pair of twins are Oscar Stör and Jack Yufe. They have also been separated since birth, and since then their lives have moved in almost completely different directions. Stow was raised by his grandmother in Czechoslovakia and entered Nazi-run schools during the Second World War; And Ufi was taken to Trinidad by his biological father and became a Jew. Stow is married, is a committed trade union participant and is keen to ski; And Ufi is separated, a businessman and considers himself a workaholic. In addition to these obvious differences, researchers found that two people were strikingly similar to some of the tiny patterns of behaviour. Both had a moustache, both looked at magazines from the back, used to wear rubber bands on their wrists, flushed toilets and then went to the toilet, liked butter toast in coffee, and found it interesting to sneeze loudly in public.

p19.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p20.original: 分开抚养的双胞胎之间惊人的相似性是否表明我们首先是基因的产物？还是基因和环境的共同作用影响了我们的毕生发展？
p20.en: Is the striking similarities between separated twins suggesting that we are first and foremost the product of genes? Or is the co-effects of genes and the environment affecting our lifelong development?

p21.original: 这些故事非常引人入胜，但是我们必须谨慎地解释它们（Phelps et al.，1997）。让我们戴上批判性思维的眼镜来审视这些解释，并提出以下几个重要的问题：
p21.en: These stories are fascinating, but we must explain them carefully (Phelps et al., 1997). Let us look at these interpretations with the glasses of critical thinking and ask the following important questions:

p22.original: 这些双胞胎的故事可以代表所有被分开抚养的双胞胎吗？还是他们只是一些特例？
p22.en: Can the story of these twins represent all the separated twins? Or are they just a few exceptions?

p23.original: 当我们留意到血缘亲属（双胞胎、兄弟姐妹、父母与子女）的惊人相似性的时候，是否发现其他不同于基因的因素可以解释这些相似性？
p23.en: When we are aware of the alarming similarities between blood relatives (twins, siblings, parents and children), do we find other factors different from genes to explain these similarities?

p24.original: 是否有一些方法帮助我们理清基因和环境二者贡献之间的差异，并且为二者的相对贡献量做一个精确的判断？
p24.en: Is there some way to help us sort out the differences between the contributions of genes and the environment and to make a precise judgement of their relative contribution?

p25.original: 先天还是后天：我们如何判断
p25.en: First or second: How do we judge?

p26.original: 这些有趣的问题只是人类毕生发展研究要探讨的部分问题。广义上说，发展心理学（developmental psychology）是研究从受孕到死亡整个过程中的成长、变化和稳定性的领域。它试图回答从婴儿期、儿童期、青春期到成年期人们的思维、感受以及行为是如何发生变化的。它从躯体、情绪、认知和社会文化多个视角来考察这些变化。因此，对于发展心理学家来说，他们要探索的主要问题有两个。在整个生命周期，个体的那些可以预测的变化是如何发生的，遗传和环境在这些变化中起什么作用？
p26.en: These interesting questions are just some of the issues that human development research has to address. Broadly speaking, developmental psychology is an area of development, change and stability throughout the entire process, from conception to death. It attempts to answer how people's thinking, feeling and behaviour have changed from infancy, childhood, adolescence to adulthood. It looks at these changes from a variety of physical, emotional, cognitive and sociocultural perspectives. Thus, for the development of psychologists, there are two main questions that they will explore. How are those predictable changes of individuals occurring throughout the life cycle, and what is the role of genetic and environmental change in these changes?

p27.original: 遗传和环境这个议题很重要，所以我们需要更加仔细地了解它。心理学家把它称为先天-后天问题（nature-nurture issue）：先天指的是遗传因素，而后天指的是环境因素。早期研究中，先天-后天是一个二选一的问题，但是现代研究人员对这个复杂问题有了更成熟的理解（Bronfenbrenner & Ceci，1994；Dannefer & Perlmutter，1990）。如今，研究人员认为，先天和后天在人类行为的几乎每一个方面都起着一定的作用，当前这个领域的问题包括：（1）每一个因素对人类不同行为的影响有多大；（2）两个因素如何互相作用，最终形成了某个特定的特征。
p27.en: The topic of genetics and the environment is important, so we need to understand it more closely. Psychologists refer to it as the natural-nurture issue: birth refers to genetic factors, whereas birth refers to environmental factors. In early research, congenital-nate issues are a matter of choice, but modern researchers have developed a more mature understanding of this complex issue (Bronfenbrenner & Cici, 1994; Danefer & Perlmutter, 1990. Today, researchers believe that the birth and the day are playing a role in almost every aspect of human behaviour, and the current problems in this area include: (1) how much each factor affects different human behaviour; (2) How the two factors interact, ultimately creating a particular characteristic.

p28.original: 那什么是相互作用呢？简单地说，先天-后天相互作用指我们生下来都具有某种潜能（先天），如果我们出生后处于合适的环境（后天）中，那么我们的潜能就会得到充分发展。例如，如果你擅长数学或音乐，你的这一能力很可能开始于某些基因的潜力，然后又得益于你的教育经历才获得发展。遗传确立了你的潜力，但是经历决定了你的潜力是否能得到发展，以及得到何种程度的发展。
p28.en: So what's the interaction? In short, the innate-nate interaction means that we are all born with a certain potential (innate), and if we are born in the right environment (innate), then our potential will be fully developed. For example, if you are good at mathematics or music, it is likely that your ability will begin with the potential of some genes and then develop through your educational experience. Genetics establish your potential, but experience determines whether and to what extent your potential can be developed.

p29.original: J.K.罗琳（J.K. Rowling）的“哈利·波特系列”的粉丝可能会发现，在哈利·波特身上也体现出先天-后天的相互作用。虽然哈利具有魔法师的纯血统（他的父母都具有魔法力），但是他是由麻瓜（不具有魔法力的人）养大的，所以一开始哈利的魔法力并没有得到充分的发挥，直到他进入霍格沃茨学校这个适宜的环境。
p29.en: J.K. Rowling's "Harry Potter" fans may find that the interaction between birth and the day after is also evident in Harry Potter. Although Harry had a pure bloodline of a magician (both his parents were magical), he was raised by Muggles (who were not magical), so at first Harry's magic was not fully exploited until he entered the proper environment at the Hogwarts School.

p30.original: 不过，我们可能还会问：“我们的哪些特质受遗传因素影响最大？哪些受学习或者其他环境因素（如疾病或营养）的影响更多？”已经有越来越多的信息可以帮助我们回答这些问题，我们将在这一章探讨这一难题。然而，我们必须谨慎地解释这些发现。例如，我们都知道在类似唐氏综合征的基因疾病中，生物因素起重要作用。在这种情况下，异常染色体导致了智力缺陷，并且这种缺陷是无法治愈的。但是，如果具有这种缺陷的小孩的父母或者老师错误地认为，他们对于生物因素导致的缺陷无能为力，那么这种生物归因就可能是有害的。过于关注这个疾病的基因因素，使得他们可能忽视基于学习的有效治疗方法，这些方法可以明显地提高患者的生活技能和各项能力。如今，表观遗传学（epigenetics）为环境如何对我们的基因基础产生实质性的影响提供了新的见解，从而证实了环境的重要作用。
p30.en: However, we might also ask, “What are our characteristics most affected by genetic factors? What are the more affected by learning or other environmental factors (e.g. disease or nutrition)? There is already a growing amount of information to help us answer these questions, and we will look at this dilemma in this chapter. However, we must carefully explain these findings. For example, we all know that biological factors play an important role in genetic diseases such as Down syndrome. In such cases, abnormal chromosomes cause intellectual impairments, which cannot be cured. However, if the parents or teachers of a child with such defects mistakenly believe that they are incapable of being able to cope with the defects caused by biological factors, then such biological attribution may be harmful. Excessive attention to the genetic factors of the disease makes it possible for them to ignore effective learning-based treatments that can significantly improve the life skills and abilities of patients. Today, the value of the environment is confirmed by the new insights that the epigenetics provide on how the environment has a substantial impact on our genetic base.

p31.original: 虽然心理学家意识到研究中存在这种错误评估的危险，但他们仍然在遗传和环境对人类思维和行为的影响这一研究领域奋勇向前。他们发明了几种巧妙的方法来评估先天因素和后天因素的影响。双生子研究（twin study）就是其中之一。例如，托马斯·布沙尔的工作就为先天和后天的相对贡献提供了一些有价值的线索：在这种情况下，双胞胎之间的任何相似性都可能是遗传的结果，因为他们的成长环境完全不同。然而，这类双胞胎是一种稀缺资源。通常，双胞胎都是一起长大的，幸运的是，心理学家已经找到了对普通双胞胎进行研究的方法。同卵双胞胎本质上拥有相同的基因，异卵双胞胎平均而言只有50%的基因是相同的，因此遗传对同卵双胞胎的影响更大。比较这两类双胞胎的研究通常把异卵双胞胎视为控制组（control group）。这类研究为我们考察基因在各种心理和行为障碍中的作用提供了有价值的线索，包括酗酒、阿尔茨海默病、精神分裂、抑郁症和孤独症（Muhle et al.，2004；Plomin et al.，1994）。
p31.en: Although psychologists are aware of the risk of such miscalculation in research, they continue to move forward in the field of research on the effects of genetic and environmental influence on human thinking and behaviour. They have developed several clever ways to assess the effects of congenital and acquired factors. The twin-child study is one of them. For example, Thomas Bouchard's work provides some valuable clues to the relative contribution of birth and birth: in such cases, any similarities between twins may be a genetic consequence, as they grow up in completely different environments. However, these twins are a scarce resource. Usually, the twins grow up together and, fortunately, the psychologist has found a way to study the normal twins. The same genes are essentially the same for the same twins, and on average only 50 per cent of the same genes are identical for the same twins, so genetics have a greater impact on the same twins. The comparison of the two types of twins is usually seen as a control group (control group). Such studies provide valuable insights into the role of genes in various psychological and behavioural disorders, including alcohol abuse, Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, depression and autism (Muhle et al., 2004); Promin et al., 1994.

p32.original: 另一种考察遗传和环境作用的方法是收养研究（adoption study）。如果你收养了一个孩子，他最终会更像谁呢？像你还是其亲生父母？收养研究比较了收养儿童的特质与他们的血亲或收养家庭成员的特质。与血亲家庭之间的相似性是先天因素的作用，而与收养家庭之间的相似性则受后天因素的影响。这类研究与双生子研究一起揭示了遗传对各种心理特质的贡献，如智力、性取向、性格和冲动行为——我们会在后续部分对所有这些内容进行更详细的叙述（Alanko et al.，et al.2010；Bouchard，1994；Dabbs，2000）。
p32.en: Another way of examining the effects of genetic and environmental effects is through adoption studies. If you adopt a child, who will he end up more like? Like you or his real parents? Adoption studies compare the characteristics of adopted children with those of their biological or adoptive family members. Similarity with the biological family is the function of congenital factors, while similarities with the adoptive family are influenced by congenital factors. Such studies, together with twin-child studies, reveal the contribution of genetics to various psychological characteristics, such as intelligence, sexual orientation, character and impulse behaviour, all of which we will describe in more detail in the follow-up section (Alanko et al., et al. 2010); Bouchard, 1994; Dabbs, 2000.
